newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ABB SEES NO LARGE ACQUISITIONS.
newsitem.headline: ABB SEES NO LARGE ACQUISITIONS.

text.p: International engineering company ABB said on Friday it would mainly grow organically in the future and that no large acquisitions were on the agenda.
"You should not expect us to make any large acquisitions... Growth will mainly be organic," ABB's chief executive Goran Lindahl told an analysts' meeting.

ABB said in its annual report that its long-term target is to reach an average annual growth of at least six percent over the next economic cycle. ABB could also sell off some more operations, Lindahl said.
The company sold operations with sales of US$300-350 million in the first half of 1997.
"I cannot exclude that we will look at (selling) more areas in the future," Lindahl said.
